headline: Record King Tides and a big incoming swell bring moderate to major, locally extreme coastal flooding through Friday (worst Thursday morning), while inland it turns warm and windy for Thanksgiving; light showers are possible Sunday night into Monday, and a stronger, possibly soaking storm may arrive around next Tuesday and Wednesday.

sections.title: Today & Tonight
sections.text: Wednesday stays dry with high clouds from a passing storm system to the north spreading over the area, then clearing Wednesday night. Highs are similar to Tuesday, mostly in the 70s along the coast and in the valleys, warmest (mid to upper 70s) from the inland coastal areas into the western valleys. Northeast winds pick up below the mountain passes Wednesday afternoon and evening, gusting roughly 30–40 mph.

sections.title: Short Term
sections.text: On Thanksgiving (Thursday) and Friday, high pressure overhead and offshore winds bring warming, with east to northeast winds gusting 35–45 mph along and below the coastal slopes of the mountains. Thanksgiving highs climb 4–8 degrees, reaching the lower to mid 80s from the inland coastal areas into the western valleys, 12–18 degrees above average, with little change Friday. The mountains and high desert warm about another 5 degrees on Friday.

sections.title: Long Term
sections.text: High clouds return Friday night and Saturday as the high pressure weakens and the cooler ocean breeze comes back. Saturday's highs drop 4–8 degrees to the mid 70s to around 80 in the coast and valleys, and cooling continues through Tuesday, when highs range from the mid 60s in the far inland valleys to around 70 at the coast. A fast-moving storm crossing California brings a chance of showers Sunday night and Monday, and a stormier pattern may follow, with a storm around Tuesday and Wednesday that could bring strong winds and heavy rain, though its timing and track are uncertain. From Tuesday morning through Thursday night, the chance of 1 inch or more of rain from the coast to the mountains is 75–85 percent in Orange and southwestern San Bernardino Counties and around 60 percent in southern San Diego County; the chance of 3 inches or more is 5–10 percent near the coast and 25–35 percent in the mountains.

coast: Coastal flooding is the main story on the Orange County and San Diego County coasts. Morning high tides of 7.9–8.3 feet are expected each day through Thursday, peaking Wednesday morning; these run 1.1–1.2 feet above normal predictions and will likely break the all-time records set just in late October (Tuesday morning's 8.46 feet at the San Diego Broadway Pier and 7.97 feet at La Jolla were each the second highest on record). Surf of 2–5 feet through Wednesday morning grows as a long-period west swell (7–8 feet every 16–18 seconds) arrives late Wednesday, producing 6–8 foot breakers Thursday with sets of 10–12 feet on exposed west-facing beaches, then easing to 3–7 feet Friday. A Coastal Flood Warning runs until 1 PM Friday for moderate to major flooding, with locally extreme flooding expected at Thursday morning's high tide, and a High Surf Advisory covers the San Diego County coast from 1 PM Wednesday to 4 AM Friday. For boaters, a Small Craft Advisory covers the outer waters (10–60 miles out from San Mateo Point to the Mexican border, including San Clemente Island) from 10 AM Wednesday to 10 AM Thursday for seas of 8–12 feet, with northwest gusts near 23 mph far offshore Wednesday afternoon; seas fall below 10 feet by Thursday evening.
watch_for: Moderate to major, locally extreme coastal flooding at the morning high tides through Friday, worst Thursday morning when record tides meet 10–12 foot surf sets.
East to northeast gusts of 35–45 mph near the coastal mountain slopes Thanksgiving and Friday, with inland highs in the lower to mid 80s.
The possible strong storm around next Tuesday–Wednesday: 1 inch or more of rain is likely, but timing, track and amounts are still uncertain.
confidence: Forecasters are confident in the dry, warm, breezy weather through the weekend and in the record tides and coastal flooding; confidence is lower in the timing, track and details of the storms next week.
